articles.title: FIDE World Chess Championship | Gukesh finds his rhythm as third-game draw sets up an exciting contest
articles.summary: Three games of the World Chess Championship between the 20-year-olds, defending champion Dommaraju Gukesh and challenger Javokhir Sindarov of Uzbekistan, have created a big buzz about their fine form and fighting spirit, despite all three games ending in deadlocks. The first rest day could not have come at a better time for Gukesh, as he demonstrated wonderful home preparation in the opening of the third game, played a lively and intriguing middle-game and showed some neat end-game prowess, apart from maintaining his momentum with the clock, which had worked against him in the first two games. Definitely the right tone and mood to head into the rest day. The champion and challenger entered Geneva, Switzerland, for the World Championship in contrasting styles, with Gukesh struggling with his form and Sindarov in blazing form. Gukesh had dropped about 60 Elo points, while Sindarov had gained 70 Elo points. Sindarov’s Uzbekistan team had won team gold at the Olympiad, while Gukesh’s India team had settled for silver. If there were many who were worried for Gukesh, Javokhir too had plenty rooting for him. Gukesh has an edge over Javokhir in terms of match experience, having played and powered his way to win the title. The first three of the 14 games scheduled may have petered out into draws, with both Gukesh and Javokhir impressing without gaining an advantage, but they have clearly hinted at the competitive character exhibited by both, which should set the tone for the remaining 11 games. Gukesh will wield White in six games and Javokhir in five. Another interesting aspect of the games played so far is the blazing level of average accuracy in terms of moves made, above 98 per cent for both. Yesterday, in the third game, Gukesh exhibited a phenomenal 99.1 per cent accuracy. FIDE World Chess Championship | Gukesh, Sindarov battle for 60 moves before settling for third-game draw The average accuracy in previous World Championship matches has fluctuated between 87 per cent and 97 per cent. Magnus Carlsen leads the dataset at 96.55 per cent (across 63 games), followed closely by Garry Kasparov (96.01 per cent over 197 games), Vladimir Kramnik (95.95 per cent) and Viswanathan Anand (95.94 per cent), according to the data released by Chess.com. Add to it the aggressive instincts of the players, which have been in the forefront, with both not hesitating to explore the option of gaining the tiniest advantage to put pressure. In terms of opening preparation, Gukesh has shown some intensive home preparation. Both players have been found wanting in clock management, Gukesh in the first two games and Javokhir in the third. Javokhir has stayed true to his King’s pawn opening with White, while Gukesh has been springing surprises, opting for the Berlin Defence in the first and third games, a defence which has not been a regular part of his opening repertoire. This is an interesting choice and brought back memories of the 2000 World Chess Championship, where Kramnik employed this opening to blunt Garry Kasparov’s aggression and dethrone him. Interestingly, Kramnik played the Berlin four times then and drew all four games, with his two victories with the White pieces winning him the World title. Gukesh, with the White pieces, baffled everyone with his choice of the ‘London System’ in Game 2, terming it a ‘cool choice’, even as most followers found it dull and uncool. Not surprisingly, the game lasted just about 20 moves, though it did have some undercurrents. The third game yesterday was the most interesting and exciting one, with fine positional understanding exhibited by both, though devoid of a decisive result. Converting an advantage into a victory is crucial, and not just reaching a promising position. Gukesh can take many positives from this game as he heads into the rest day and prepares to play fresh with the White pieces in the fourth game on Saturday.

articles.title: Winter skincare: Simple ways to keep your skin healthy and glowing
articles.summary: As temperatures dip, your skin may feel tight, itchy and dry. Winter skincare is less about adding products and more about understanding what your skin needs. Here are some steps to achieving glowing skin during the winter months. Moisturising is not optional Your skin has a protective barrier that retains moisture and keeps irritants out. Cooler weather, lower humidity and long, hot showers can disrupt it, causing dryness, flaking and sometimes eczema flare-ups. Even mild Bengaluru winters can affect skin health. Post-festive skincare: After the sparkle, comes the glow Choose products with ceramides, glycerin, hyaluronic acid or petrolatum. Apply moisturiser just after bathing while your skin is slightly damp. A rich cream may suit very dry skin better than a lotion. Remember your hands, feet, elbows and legs. Use a fragrance-free, petrolatum-based lip balm, and moisturise your hands after washing and at bedtime. Rethink bathing Hot showers feel comforting but can worsen dryness. Use lukewarm water, keep showers short and choose gentle cleansers. Avoid vigorous scrubbing, loofahs and frequent exfoliation. Sunscreen still matters UV radiation does not disappear in winter. Choose broad-spectrum SPF 30 or higher. Tinted sunscreen with iron oxides may be especially helpful for melasma and pigmentation concerns. Adjust active ingredients Retinoids and exfoliating acids can sting when the skin barrier is irritated. Consider using them less frequently and increasing moisturisation. Healthy skin does not entail expensive products. Gentle cleansing, regular moisturising and sun protection are the essentials. Persistent itching, painful cracks or inflammation need a dermatologist’s attention. (The author is a consultant dermatologist)

articles.title: New Bill fixes delimitation oversight, allows UP Assembly to expand to 605 seats
articles.summary: New Delhi: An oversight by the Modi government in the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, introduced in April this year, which would have deprived Uttar Pradesh of a 50 per cent increase in Assembly seats, has been rectified in the new Bill by raising the maximum limit of seats from 500 to 650. Uttar Pradesh has 403 Assembly seats and, under the earlier version of the Bill, which was defeated in the Lok Sabha in April, it could not have increased its strength to 605 seats. The previous Bill had not proposed amending the provision that capped the number of Assembly seats at 500. However, the Constitution (132nd Amendment) Bill, 2026, which will be tabled in the Lok Sabha on Monday, mandates an increase in the maximum number of Assembly seats to 650, enabling Uttar Pradesh to have a 50 per cent increase in seats. In the Lok Sabha, the State's seats will rise from 80 to 120, the highest for any State in the country. Uttar Pradesh was the only State that would have been affected if the ceiling had remained at 500. West Bengal has the second-highest number of Assembly seats at 294, and a 50 per cent increase would have taken its tally to 441. Centre confident of numbers to pass delimitation bills linked to women’s reservation In the Statement of Reasons for Withdrawal of the Delimitation Bill, 2026, the government has admitted that the previous Bill had overlooked the impact of delimitation on the representation of various States in the Lok Sabha due to variations in population growth. During discussions on the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026, concerns were raised, according to the statement to be tabled in the Lok Sabha, about “the possible impact of the proposed delimitation exercise on the representation of different states” in the Lok Sabha, “particularly in view of the variations in population growth across the country”. “The government has examined these issues with a view to ensuring that the constitutional framework for the next delimitation exercise is clear, balanced and capable of addressing the concerns raised while preserving the representative character,” it said. A “uniform increase” in Lok Sabha seats across States would “enhance the overall representation of people while maintaining the existing relative distribution of seats among states”, it said. While three Bills - one to amend the Constitution to increase seats and roll out the 33 per cent women's quota, another to set up a delimitation commission, and a third to implement a similar increase in seats in Union Territories - were part of the April package, the government has now introduced just two Bills by expanding the definition of States in Article 55 to include the Union Territories of Jammu and Kashmir, Delhi and Puducherry. This amendment to Article 55 means that there would be no need for a separate Bill to implement the constitutional amendments in the Union Territories.

articles.title: Draft delimitation Bill released: 50% increase in seats, 850-seat Lok Sabha, freeze till 2051
articles.summary: The Union government has released the draft Constitution (One Hundred and Thirty-Second Amendment) Bill, 2026, which proposes the delimitation of constituencies based on the latest Census. All states shall see a 50% increase in the number of Lok Sabha and Legislative Assembly seats. According to the draft Bill, delimitation of Lok Sabha and Legislative Assembly constituencies’ boundaries will be done as per the latest Census figures, and will be frozen again until 2051. The Bill expands the maximum strength of the Lok Sabha from 550 to 850. Under Article 81 of the Constitution, the upper limit for total members representing constituencies from the states will be raised from 530 to 815. For union territories, the number will go up from 20 to 35. The composition of each state Assembly, previously capped at 500, has been proposed to go up to 650 MLAs. The Bill text frames delimitation as a constitutional requirement to implement 33% reservation for women in Lok Sabha and state Assemblies. It says, “The implementation of reservation of seats for women is linked to the constitutional scheme of readjustment in the allocation of seats in the House of the People and the Legislative Assemblies and re-drawing boundaries of territorial constituencies by the Delimitation Commission.” The Delimitation Commission, as defined in the Election Commission of India website, is a high power body whose orders have the force of law and cannot be called in question before any court. The Constitution Amendment Bill is to be tabled in the Lok Sabha on Monday, November 30, in a special sitting announced by the Union government on November 26. The BJP’s previous attempt to pass the delimitation Bill was defeated in the Lok Sabha in April. For a Constitution Amendment Bill to be passed, it requires a two-thirds majority among the members present and voting. The Constitution (One Hundred and Thirty-First Amendment) Bill, 2026, was defeated with 211 out of 489 members who were present voting against it. This was during a special session convened while election campaigns were underway in several states. With the political atmosphere having changed since the election results were declared, the BJP hopes to get the required two-thirds majority of those present and voting. Back then, the Bill did not include a written provision to increase the seats for each state uniformly and not on the basis of population, but simply proposed increasing the total strength of the Lok Sabha to 850. Though Union Home Minister Amit Shah had given an oral assurance in this regard, MPs from multiple states objected, seeking the provision in writing. When asked for the reason behind expanding the Lok Sabha to 850 seats, Amit Shah had said that the idea was to expand the previous Lok Sabha by 50% so that when one-third of the seats set aside for women were accounted for, the remaining two-thirds strength would be similar to the original strength which are occupied predominantly by men. The DMK and NCP are likely to support the bill as 50% increase and a 25 year freeze are among their primary demands. With political defections of Members of Parliament from TMC, AAP and Shiv Sena (UBT), the NDA’s numbers have been bolstered.

articles.title: Karnataka to see no seat hike, women’s quota in 2028 polls; changes only post-2029
articles.summary: New Delhi: If the NDA government succeeds in pushing through its delimitation-linked 33 per cent women’s reservation bills in Parliament next week, Karnataka is unlikely to see any change in the number of assembly seats when it heads to the polls in May 2028. A uniform 50 per cent increase in both Lok Sabha and state assembly seats across the country — is expected to take effect only with the 2029 Lok Sabha elections and in assembly elections held after that, sources said. The bills, once passed by Parliament, will trigger the formation of a Delimitation Commission by the Election Commission . That process of redrawing parliamentary and assembly constituencies is projected to stretch into the end of 2028. With Karnataka’s assembly elections due in May 2028, the state will therefore contest on the existing number of seats and women reservation will not be applicable. Only those states going to the polls after the May-June 2029 Lok Sabha elections will see the expanded constituencies with women reservation, sources said. If the uniform 50 per cent rise in Assembly seats happens, in Karnataka the total number of seats will go up to 336 from existing 224 seats. Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister and TDP leader N Chandrababu Naidu, addressing the media alongside Union Steel Minister and JD(S) leader H D Kumaraswamy, confirmed the sequencing. “All assembly polls held after the 2029 Lok Sabha elections will have the increased seats,” Naidu said. He added that, like the Lok Sabha, every state and Union Territory will see its assembly seats rise by 50 per cent from the current strength. Delimitation: BJP MPs should stop being Modi’s yes-men, says Siddaramaiah The Union Cabinet has cleared a fresh version of the bill with amendments designed to ensure no state loses its relative representation in the Lok Sabha after delimitation. To allay long-standing concerns of southern states, the government has agreed to raise Lok Sabha seats by 50 per cent across every state rather than redistributing them purely on population. A freeze on further changes is proposed until 2051. The redrawing will be based on the 2011 Census and will keep the percentage share of seats for each state largely intact. Naidu and Kumaraswamy, both the NDA partners, sought to reassure southern leaders that the formula avoids the injustice many had feared. “Since the government has agreed to increase the seats by 50 per cent from the existing Lok Sabha strength in every state, there will not be any injustice to any state, particularly the southern states,” Naidu said. Under the proposed expansion, the five southern states would see their combined strength rise from 129 seats in the current 543-member House to 195 seats in an 816-member House. Karnataka’s tally would move from 28 to 42, Tamil Nadu from 39 to 59, Andhra Pradesh from 25 to 38, Keralam from 20 to 30, and Telangana from 17 to 26. Their collective share would remain virtually unchanged — from 23.76 per cent now to roughly 23.87 per cent in the larger House. The timeline means Karnataka’s 2028 contest will still be fought under the present map. For other states whose assembly elections fall after the next general election, the expanded numbers — and the women’s reservation that travels with them — will become reality.

articles.title: 'More lifelike, intimidating' langur cut-outs return to NDMC neighbourhoods to keep monkeys at bay
articles.summary: New Delhi: In a fresh bid to tackle the monkey menace in the capital's most prominent neighbourhoods, the New Delhi Municipal Council (NDMC) is bringing back langur cut-outs — this time with a more realistic and intimidating appearance, as the pesky primates had 'grown accustomed' to the earlier versions. Officials said the civic body has redesigned the life-size cut-outs of grey langurs and began installing them across NDMC areas on Thursday, covering public spaces as well as locations identified following requests from residents and government establishments. "Residents regularly approach us with complaints about monkeys in their neighbourhoods. We are putting up the cut-outs at public places on our own as well as at locations from where we receive requests. The new models have been made more realistic and intimidating," an NDMC official said. The initial locations include Charak Palika Hospital, Connaught Place , Teen Murti, B K Dutt Colony and areas around the prime minister's office, following requests from respective establishments. The latest exercise follows an experiment in 2023, when the civic body installed similar cut-outs to deter rhesus macaques, commonly known as rhesus monkeys. However, the measure gradually lost its effectiveness as the animals became familiar with the static figures. "Monkeys are intelligent animals, and they eventually realised that the cut-outs were not real. The earlier models therefore became ineffective. This time, we have made them look more lifelike and scary so that they can act as a deterrent," the official said. The NDMC also caught 32 monkeys from Connaught Place on Friday as part of its efforts to control their population in public areas. Alongside langur cut-outs, the civic body is putting up awareness posters asking people not to feed monkeys in public spaces. The posters will also carry helpline numbers through which residents can report sightings and seek assistance. NDMC Director (Administration) Arun Gupta has distributed the newly designed cut-outs and awareness posters to field supervisors for installation at suitable locations, according to a social media post. In 2024, the NDMC engaged an agency under a one-year contract to catch 1,000 monkeys at a rate of Rs 1,800 per primate. The target was achieved within three months, following which the civic body began deploying its regular employees for the task. "After the contract, our regular employees also started catching monkeys. We have made cages for the purpose and have a dedicated vehicle to carry out the operations," the official said. Ahead of the G20 Summit in August 2023, the NDMC had installed langur cut-outs along the Central Ridge and major roads to prevent monkeys from straying into areas frequented by visiting dignitaries. The exercise was also accompanied by the deployment of around 30-40 trained personnel to mimic langur calls. Delhi has never conducted a census of its monkey population, even as sightings and attacks have remained a recurring civic concern. In one of the most serious incidents, then deputy mayor S S Bajwa died in 2007 after monkeys attacked him on the terrace of his residence, causing him to fall and sustain fatal head injuries. Following the incident and directions from the Delhi High Court, the Municipal Corporation of Delhi began catching monkeys and relocating them to the Asola Bhatti Wildlife Sanctuary.

articles.title: Govt lines up 3 bills to roll out women's quota, expand House seats by 50%
articles.summary: New Delhi: The government is confident of passage of the bills for implementing women's reservation in Lok Sabha and State Assemblies as major changes have been made to win support of parties like DMK and NCP (SP), which had vehemently opposed the earlier bill that got defeated in April, official sources said Friday. The government will bring three bills — one of them Constitution amendment — for the implementation of 33 per cent women's reservation in the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies before the 2029 parliamentary elections, while explicitly mentioning a 50 per cent increase in seats for each state. Official sources said the government is confident of passage of these bills. Centre confident of numbers to pass delimitation bills linked to women’s reservation "We are supremely confident that the three bills will be passed this time. We have already consulted many parties and their leaders and only after we got full assurance that we have decided to convened the special sitting," a source said. While Lok Sabha seats will be increased up to a maximum of 850 with parliamentary constituencies of each state will be increased by 50 per cent, barring a few Union territories. The boundaries of Lok Sabha and Assembly seats will be reconstituted on the basis of 2011 census but the ratio of constituencies will be determined on the basis of 1971 census, the sources said. Explained | What is delimitation? Why is the Bill pending, and what is the debate about? This has been done to allay any apprehension of the southern states which fear that they may lose out if the boundaries are determined on the basis of current population as they have been successful in population control, unlike northern states, they said. The DMK has made it clear that under no circumstances should Tamil Nadu's existing 7.18 per cent share of seats in Lok Sabha be reduced. "DMK's demands will be honoured," the source said. Lok Sabha and Assembly constituencies will be frozen for 25 years — till 2051. Union Cabinet clears fresh delimitation-linked women quota bill Initially the constituencies will be reserved for 15 years (like SC & ST seats initially reserved for 10 years after adoption of Constitution) and after every term, the women seats will be rotated. Reservation of women seats after 15 years is expected to be extended by the government of the day. The second bill is for redrawing Lok Sabha and assembly constituencies and the third bill for the Union territories. Sources said that the new bill for redrawing the constituencies is hugely different than the one defeated in Lok Sabha in April. There will be massive amendments — at least in eight Articles of the Constitution. In case of smaller Union territories like Lakshadweep, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, the 50 per cent increase of constituencies will not be applicable but the formula is likely to be implemented in states like Nagaland or Mizoram where the number of seats will be increased from one to two. This will be a political decision and that is why the bill would mention that the maximum Lok Sabha seats will be up to 850. A delimitation commission will be immediately constituted to facilitate the process fast. Even though ratification of the Constitution amendments bills by 50 per cent State Assemblies is not mandatory, the Modi government will do it as part of the convention. As part of the government plans, it will first withdraw the two bills — delimitation and UT — currently the properties of the Lok Sabha. After their withdrawal, the three new bills will be introduced for debate and passage. Sources said that about 10-12 hours will be expected to be allotted for debate and about five hours for voting.

Lesser florcian recorded for the first time in coastal Karnataka
articles.summary: Hubballi: The field staff of Ankola forest range recorded the presence of one of the most critical birds — the lesser florican — for the first time in coastal Karnataka on Friday. Lesser floricans are a grassland birds and their population has drastically dwindled due to habitat loss and poaching. The birds, once a common sight in the northern plains of Karnataka, are now limited to Bidar and some grasslands of central Karnataka. Birds start arriving early at Ranganathittu bird sanctuary The frontline staff — C R Naik, Yamanappa B H and Chidambar V Marathi — recorded this female florican in the grasslands of Ankola in Uttara Kannada district. Experts say this could be the first time the bird was recorded in the coastal area. “Two days ago we received a camera from Kali Tiger Reserve’s Wildlife Research and Training Centre. We were experimenting with it, when Naik sighted an unusual bird among lapwings. Experts have confirmed it as lesser florican,” says Chidambar. Wildlife Institute of India scientist Mohib Uddin, who are researching on Lesser florcians, said there were earlier reports of the bird being sighted in North and Central Karnataka. “There have been records of this birds being sighted in the grasslands of coastal areas in Gujarat. However, this is probably first time that the bird was sighted in grasslands of Karnataka. This is not a bird that WII is tracking,” he said.

articles.title: Tech workers' woes: IBM ends US visa, green card sponsorship for most roles in consulting unit
articles.summary: New Delhi Global tech giant IBM is discontinuing US visa and green card sponsorship for most roles in its consulting business, its largest division with over 150,000 employees. The move comes at a time when companies based in the US are increasingly facing pressure from the government over their use of work visas, and reliance on foreign workers. "IBM Consulting participates in US high-skilled visa programmes to address skill shortages. That participation has been declining for a number of years, and as skill availability and client needs have evolved, we have opted to discontinue visa and green card sponsorship for the majority of such roles in IBM Consulting,” the company said in a statement. IBM to end H-1B, Green Card sponsorship for most consulting roles. Who will be affected and how? IBM ends US visa sponsorship, gives H-1B workers three weeks to relocate or leave company While the tech giant didn't offer further details, affected employees have reportedly been offered a choice between relocating to a country outside the US or leaving the company by the end of the year. According to posts by employees on anonymous professional discussion platform Blind, some affected employees have been given about three weeks to decide, with three months' severance for those who decline an overseas role and December 31 as their last working day, “I got pulled into a surprise meeting with my manager and was told I have just three weeks to choose between taking an 80 per cent pay cut to relocate to India or losing my job by December 31. I've spent years building my career here, working long hours for IBM clients, paying taxes and building a life in the US. Now I'm being told to either uproot everything or walk away with just three months of severance,” an employee wrote on Blind. Over the past years, US tech giants are facing increased scrutiny over reliance on foreign workers, deepening the uncertainty for an industry where employees across companies are facing the threat of AI displacement. In September 2026, US President Donald Trump extended by a year the $100,000 fee on employers for bringing in foreign workers on H-1B visas. He said the 2025 decision to impose a $100,000 fee has led to a 92 per cent decrease in H-1B registrations by large IT outsourcing firms. An extension of the 2025 Proclamation will continue to protect the economic and national security interests of the United States, improve labour market access for American workers and graduates, and ensure that employers recruit only the most highly skilled and essential alien workers when needed in line with the original intent of the programme, Trump said. Indians remain the single largest beneficiary group of the US H-1B visa programme.

articles.title: Only about 20-30% Indian exports take advantage of lower FTA tariffs: RBI Governor
articles.summary: Bengaluru: Only about 20-30 per cent of eligible Indian exports take advantage of the lower tariffs available under various free trade agreements (FTAs) signed by the central government, Reserve Bank of India ( RBI ) Governor Sanjay Malhotra said on Friday, asking businesses to look beyond domestic markets for their expansion. Malhotra said Indian businesses taking advantage of FTAs is “remarkably low” as 60–70 per cent of eligible exports from the partner countries utilise the benefits. Fed paused, prices didn’t: Why RBI must keep its tightening bias “It is an opportunity we are leaving on the table. Learn about the FTAs relevant to your products, invest in quality, standards and certification, and draw on the support available from the agencies concerned,” he said at SME Finance & Investment summit held in Mumbai. The RBI Governor said that India’s expanding network of free trade agreements, some with dedicated chapters on small and medium enterprises (SMEs), opens up new markets abroad. “It improves access to quality inputs at lower cost and offers the chance to specialise in niche segments of global value chains. Labour-intensive MSME sectors, in particular, can be important conduits through which the benefits of trade are realised,” he added. The RBI governor’s remarks came days after Prime Minister Narendra Modi urged Indian business to actively capitalise on the FTAs and expand into overseas markets rather than relying solely on the domestic markets. articles.title: Kerala CPI(M) caught in a bind over former MLA's remarks on political killings
articles.summary: A speech by Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)] leader and former MLA TI Madhusoodanan, invoking the 1987 Cheemeni killings while warning the party's critics of consequences, has brought the Left's position on political violence back into focus in Keralam. On November 27, Friday, CPI(M) state secretary M V Govindan reiterated that the party opposed political killings, while Communist Party of India (CPI) state secretary Binoy Viswam said murder could never be a means of Communist politics. The remarks come as the police investigate Madhusoodanan's speech. A member of the CPI(M)'s Kannur district secretariat, Madhusoodanan made the comments at a programme organised by the Democratic Youth Federation of India (DYFI) in Payyannur on November 25, following the verdict in the 2016 murder of CPI(M) activist C V Dhanarajan. The Taliparamba Additional Sessions Court sentenced three workers of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) and the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) to life imprisonment in the case, while acquitting 16 others. Referring to the 1987 Cheemeni killings, in which five CPI(M) workers were hacked to death and burnt inside a party office, Madhusoodanan said that although no one had been punished by a court in the case, none of those involved was alive today. "No court punished anyone in the Cheemeni incident, where five people were burnt to death. But the establishment would do well to understand that none of them exists on this earth today. Not even one," he said. His remarks were widely interpreted as a veiled threat of retaliation against those acquitted in the Dhanarajan murder case. He also warned those criticising the CPI(M) on social media against taking their criticism to the streets, saying they would face consequences. He reportedly said the party would not hesitate to visit the homes of those who insulted it. Madhusoodanan also launched an attack on the judge who delivered the Dhanarajan murder verdict, accusing the judiciary of attempting to suppress progressive and Left-wing politics through imprisonment and punishment. Referring sarcastically to the judgment, he said it was fortunate that the court had not declared that Dhanarajan had never been murdered. He questioned the court's rejection of the testimony of a key witness in the case and took a swipe at Payyannur MLA V Kunhikrishnan, who had earlier fallen out with the CPI(M), calling him a "political eunuch". Left parties reiterate stand Speaking to reporters on November 27, Govindan said the CPI(M) did not endorse murder politics or any provocative stance associated with it. He said the party had consistently maintained that no one should be killed in the name of political differences, pointing to the position adopted at its 2018 Thrissur conference. “The party has made it clear that there should be no political killings. This was our position at the 2018 Thrissur conference as well. No one should be killed in Keralam in the name of politics,” he said. Govindan also said that Keralam had witnessed a relatively peaceful atmosphere over the past decade and that the party remained committed to maintaining it. CPI state secretary Binoy Viswam also spoke against political violence, saying that murder could never be a means of political struggle, irrespective of who made such statements. “The path of politics is one of ideological struggle. The CPI does not consider murder a means of Communist politics,” he said. He added that threats of murder, settling scores, and glorifying violence were contrary to Communist principles. "The Communist path is one of love. Communism is another name for love for humanity. That is the CPI’s conviction," he said. Police register case The Payyannur police registered a case against Madhusoodanan on Thursday, November 26, following a complaint by Kerala Students’ Union (KSU) state vice-president P Mohammed Shammas to the State Police Chief. The case was registered under Sections 192, 351(3), and 352 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), relating to provocation with intent to cause a riot, criminal intimidation, and intentional insult with intent to provoke a breach of peace respectively. In his complaint, Shammas alleged that Madhusoodanan’s speech contained threats, incitement to violence, and attempts to intimidate the judiciary. He also sought an examination of the complete video recording of the speech. Earlier, Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala had said that the government viewed the remarks seriously and that the police were collecting the full text of the speech to determine what legal action could be taken. “Justifying murders taking place in the state and calling for the killing of others are actions unbecoming of a people’s representative. Neither the police nor the government will accept such conduct,” Chennithala said, calling on the CPI(M) leadership to intervene in the matter. CPI(M) targets Satheesan Govindan, meanwhile, accused the Congress and the media of applying double standards in their response to statements that could be seen as encouraging political violence. He questioned why Chief Minister V D Satheesan had not faced similar scrutiny for his recent ‘blood for blood’ remark. Satheesan had made the remark while speaking at a programme in Kannur on November 20, referring to attacks on Youth Congress workers during the previous Left Democratic Front (LDF) government's tenure. He had said that the blood shed by Youth Congress workers would be avenged. “What does blood for blood mean? It means sparing no one, seeking revenge and demanding retribution. The Chief Minister of Keralam openly says blood for blood. This amounts to a violation of the oath of office," Govindan said. The CPI(M) has demanded that a case be registered against Satheesan as well, with Govindan arguing that the Chief Minister's position made the remark particularly serious. The DYFI has also filed a police complaint against him. The controversy has once again brought attention to Keralam's history of political violence, particularly in Kannur, where the CPI(M) and the RSS-BJP have been involved in decades of political clashes and retaliatory killings.

articles.title: 'Ensure an effective mechanism to recover unclaimed assets': Supreme Court tells authorities
articles.summary: New Delhi: The Supreme Court on Friday said authorities must ensure that mechanisms for recovering unclaimed financial assets remain effective, transparent and accessible, emphasising that the right to reclaim money would be meaningless if rightful owners cannot trace their assets or are burdened with cumbersome procedures. “The existence of a statutory right to reclaim money would be of little practical value if the persons entitled thereto are unable to trace the assets or are confronted with unnecessarily cumbersome procedures for establishing their claims,” a bench of Justices Vikram Nath and R Mahadevan said. The court said the right to property, though no longer a fundamental right, continues to enjoy constitutional protection under Article 300A of the Constitution. “The transfer of unclaimed financial assets to statutory funds does not, by itself, extinguish the rights of persons lawfully entitled thereto,” it said, adding that the State and regulatory authorities have a responsibility to facilitate recovery by rightful claimants. Victims must get a hearing before remission of convicts, says Supreme Court The court, however, said procedures must balance ease of recovery with safeguards against fraudulent or competing claims. The observations came in a judgment which disposed of a public interest litigation filed by journalist Sucheta Dalal seeking a centralised mechanism to trace and recover unclaimed bank deposits, insurance proceeds and other financial assets. The bench declined to direct the creation of a single portal, holding that existing sector-specific mechanisms, including the Reserve Bank of India's UDGAM portal, SEBI's MITRA platform and the integrated Investor Education and Protection Fund (IEPF) portal, had substantially addressed the concerns raised in the petition. The court noted that UDGAM, launched in August 2023, had expanded to 30 banks, covering nearly 90% of unclaimed deposits in the Depositor Education and Awareness Fund by value. Nearly 20 lakh users had registered and 44 lakh searches had been conducted by April 2026. It also took note of SEBI's MITRA platform, which helps investors trace inactive mutual fund folios, and the IEPF portal's reforms to simplify recovery of unclaimed dividends and securities. The Centre informed the court that amendments to banking laws now permit up to four nominees and RBI guidelines provide for settlement of death claims within 15 days of receiving complete documents. About Rs 6,453 crore in unclaimed assets had been returned to claimants as of April 18, 2026. Declining a general investigation into alleged violations of RBI directions by banks, the court said the allegations did not establish specific illegality warranting an inquiry. It also refused continuing judicial monitoring, observing that substantial corrective measures had been undertaken. The bench appreciated Dalal's efforts, observing that the petition was filed to protect the financial interests of depositors, investors and their lawful claimants. “The concerns raised were genuine,” it said.

articles.title: Need to be strong within to shut the noise: Sai Pallavi on scrutiny around portrayal of Sita
articles.summary: Mumbai: Actor Sai Pallavi on Friday said portraying Sita in Ramayana has been a deeply personal experience and addressed the social media scrutiny over her casting in the film. In the first instalment of the two-part cinematic adaptation of the Indian epic, Pallavi featured alongside Ranbir Kapoor , who featured as Lord Ram, Ravie Dubey in the role of Lakshman and Yash as Ravana, among others “My life has always been about moving from one movie to another. It does bring some sort of a change to you because you carry a bit of the role in your heart. I’ve had a few changes (in me), but they all are very personal, and I don’t think it is something that the world would understand or should even know. It is not even a bigger deal,” the actor said when asked how her life has changed after playing Sita. 'Playing Lord Rama will help him in life': Imtiaz Ali hails Ranbir Kapoor's performance in 'Ramayana' Pallavi was in conversation with Barkha Dutt at the We the Women event here. The actor, who primarily works in Tamil, Telugu, and Malayalam films, also addressed online scrutiny surrounding her casting and appearance as Sita. “I’m not blind to social media things that are out there, like, ‘Sita ma, how pretty she should look’, and all of that, but if it shakes your core, then I think the flaw lies there, and you need to get stronger,” she said. “I think I’m as secure as any human being can be, and opinions are opinions. So, growing up if you’ve some sort of insecurity, you just need to make sure you are strong within, and you can fight the rest of the world or shut the noise out,” she added. When asked about the characters she wouldn’t want to essay, the 34-year-old actor said she refuses to play characters reduced to being just a glamorous face. “If it is just going to be a part that is used as a tool for glamour or something that is replaceable, I wouldn’t want to be that. I always look for strength in a character. So, over time, when you put your foot down and you do not want to do certain things, that itself speaks for itself, and after that you start getting roles that have some substance,” she said, adding that it was difficult to reject such roles in the beginning of her career. Pallavi further said that from her decade-long career, she spent nearly four to five years sitting and waiting patiently for meaningful characters to come her way rather than accepting conventional commercial roles. “At that time, each day would feel painful; you don’t know whether roles written are good or everybody happens to be doing certain things which seem okay, so should I give in. Then I would think will I be able to live with myself after that film is out. It is not easy,” she said. Supreme Court declines urgent hearing on plea alleging distortions in 'Ramayana' Unlike most mainstream stars, Pallavi continues to function without a manager or an entourage, a choice she said stems from wanting to remain accessible to filmmakers. “When it comes to cinema, it is all about making it simple, being approachable to directors and actors, and not makу it a hard and intimidating process to get the stories across. I think having a middleman or a support could help, but I like it this way. I’m quite somebody who likes to do everything myself, so in that way this works for me.” Speaking about the expectations surrounding women's appearance on screen, the actor said the lack of diverse representation of women had influenced her perception of beauty. “If I had seen some actors who were themselves, maybe I would not have felt conscious. The male actors are usually seen in different sizes, ages, and surviving, and when you look at women, they always seem to be perfect. So, when it is your turn, and I’m in a place where I think I should stand up for something, which I thought should have been there at some point of time (referring to her no make-up look),” Pallavi said.

articles.summary: Yavatmal: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leader Abhijeet Dipke on Thursday said the Maharashtra government has offered only Rs 5,000 to drought-stricken farmers while ministers spend more money on their dogs. He also said that all political parties that are serious about women's reservation should field 50 per cent women candidates in upcoming State Assembly elections. Dipke and CJP co-convenor Ashutosh Ranka visited Yavatmal district to understand farmers' distress in Vidarbha and Marathwada regions. 85% of Maharashtra declared drought-hit, farmers to get Rs 5,000 aid before Diwali: CM Fadnavis "After listening to farmers, I realise how insensitive the government is. They are saying that they pay insurance premiums, but do not receive insurance money," Dipke said. Some farmers had not even received the Rs 5,000 assistance announced by Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis during Diwali, he claimed. "What will Rs 5,000 do for a farmer? All these ministers, MLAs and MPs spend more than Rs 5,000 on their dogs and they give farmers only Rs 5,000? They are insulting farmers... And for how many more months are they supposed to manage with this Rs 5,000?" Dipke asked. Some farmers told him that they would not even have food after a month or two, the CJP leader said. "Show a little sensitivity. At least treat them as human beings. You spend so much on your dogs, and you give farmers even less money than that. We are living in 2026," Dipke said. When Maharashtra had a terrible drought in 1972, science had not advanced so much and India had less resources. But now in spite of scientific progress and innovation, farmers are still at the mercy of nature, he said. "If nature does not cooperate, should farmers commit suicide?.....If farmers are supposed to remain completely dependent on nature, then why do we elect a government?" Dipke said. To a question on the women's reservation bill, he asked why the quota for women should remain limited to 33 per cent. As women account for half the population, political parties should give 50 percent of tickets to women in the upcoming elections, he said. "Give tickets to women in Uttar Pradesh, Punjab and Uttarakhand. All parties that are serious and sincere about women’s reservation should give tickets to women first. How many women are there in your cabinet? Just one, and you talk about women’s representation?" Dipke said.

articles.title: 21 elephants cross back into Belur taluk from Mudigere
articles.summary: Chikkamagaluru: Twenty-one of the 39 elephants that had entered the Mudigere taluk from Belur have crossed back into Belur taluk, three days after the Karnataka Forest Department temporarily suspended Operation Gaja. The herd has split into two groups, with the remaining 18 elephants staying at a coffee estate in Kannapura in the Mudigere taluk. The Forest Department had launched Operation Gaja 10 days ago to drive 56 elephants from Belur taluk towards the Bhadra Tiger Reserve. Thirty-nine elephants had entered the Mudigere taluk early Sunday morning (November 22). Tuskers split into 4 groups after capture operation halted However, the operation was suspended on Tuesday (November 24) after three MLAs announced at a press conference that they would resign, since they were not consulted before initiating the operation. “The forest department is behaving as if only the lives in Hassan district matter. We are elected by the people and we are answerable to the people. It looks like our party’s government is not honouring the views of its own MLAs. Then there is no point in continuing as MLA,” Mudigere Congress MLA Nayana Motamma had said. The elephants, which remain inside estates during the day and move to other locations at night, began moving back towards Belur on Tuesday night. By Friday morning, 21 of them had crossed Mudigere taluk and reached the area near Kannahalli in Belur taluk. Forest personnel are monitoring their movements and taking precautions to prevent them from entering residential areas. Meanwhile, Bhima, the lead elephant that has been guiding the herd, has returned towards Mudigere. Forest officials said it may lead the remaining 18 elephants near Kannapura towards Bikkodu. Meanwhile, an operation to capture a lone tusker spotted near Mattavara on the outskirts of Chikkamagaluru town began on Friday. However, the operation was unsuccessful as the elephant fled towards a hill after spotting the trained elephants brought in for the operation. Forest personnel initially planned to tranquilise the tusker. However, as it was facing the hilly terrain, officials decided to bring it towards an open area before attempting to tranquilise it. During an attempt to drive the elephant towards the open ground with the help of trained elephants, a brief confrontation took place between the trained and lone tusker. The elephant, identified as Ayyappa, knocked down a mahout before fleeing towards the hill. Forest personnel continued their efforts to capture the animal until evening but called off the operation as it had disappeared into thick bushes. The operation is scheduled to resume on Saturday morning. articles.summary: New Delhi: The Union Cabinet on Friday cleared a fresh bill linking the rollout of women's reservation to delimitation to effect a uniform 50 per cent rise in Lok Sabha seats in all states, which it is likely to introduce during the special sitting of Parliament next week. As the four-day special sitting brings the spotlight back on the delimitation debate, here's an explainer on how Parliamentary and Assembly constituencies are redrawn following such an exercise. 1. What is delimitation? Delimitation is the act or process of fixing limits or boundaries of territorial constituencies in a country or a province having a legislative body. 2. Who decides boundaries? The task of delimitation is assigned to a high-powered body known as the delimitation commission or a boundary commission. In India, such commissions have been constituted four times under the Delimitation Commission Act – in 1952, 1963, 1973 and in 2002. The Delimitation Commission of India is a high-powered body whose orders have the force of law and cannot be called in question before any court. The orders come into force on a date to be specified by the President. The copies of its orders are laid before Parliament and the state Assemblies concerned, but no modifications are permissible by them. 3. What is the debate about? The government brought 'The Delimitation Bill, 2026' to replace the 2002 law during a special sitting of Parliament in April this year, under which the Centre would have the power to constitute a delimitation commission to distribute seats in the Lok Sabha and Assemblies based on the "latest census figures". 4. Why is the Bill pending? Since the Constitution Amendment Bill relating to the implementation of the women's quota law before the 2029 general elections was defeated in the Lok Sabha in April due to a lack of numbers, the delimitation Bill never came up for voting. The government had decided to keep it pending in the Lower House. 5. What does the Bill say? Several of the provisions of the new delimitation bill are similar to the 2002 law, which would be repealed. According to the Bill, the Central government may, from time to time, by notification, constitute a body to be called the Delimitation Commission. The Commission shall comprise the following: one member, who shall be a person who is or has been a judge of the Supreme Court, to be appointed by the Centre as the chairperson of the Commission; the chief election commissioner or an election commissioner nominated by the chief election commissioner, ex officio; and the state election commissioner of the concerned state, ex officio. YSRCP to support delimitation Bill if it provides for a 50% increase in seats The Central government may, by notification, specify the term of the Commission. It may, on the request of the Commission, extend its term by such further period as it may consider necessary. The Election Commission shall act as the Delimitation Commission for the purpose of delimiting constituencies in the Assembly of Jammu and Kashmir falling under the occupation of Pakistan, when the area of the Union territory under the occupation of Pakistan ceases to be so occupied. The Bill also states that the Commission shall associate with itself for the purpose of assisting it in its duties in respect of each state, 10 persons, 5 of whom shall be members of the House of the People representing that state and 5 shall be members of the Assembly of that state. 6. What is the Opposition's stand? The opposition parties have cited the delimitation exercises in Assam and Jammu and Kashmir to raise apprehensions over gerrymandering, which refers to the manipulation of constituency boundaries for electoral advantage. The Lok Sabha Leader of Opposition, Rahul Gandhi , has accused the BJP of seeking to redraw the country's electoral map to its advantage ahead of the 2029 general elections. The government has rejected the apprehensions. Even if the existing share of states in the Lok Sabha is protected, the manner in which constituency boundaries are to be redrawn within states remains a point of contention for the opposition parties. Rajya Sabha Leader of Opposition, Mallikarjun Kharge, has invited all the opposition floor leaders for a meeting at his residence on Saturday to devise a joint strategy in view of the government's likely move to reintroduce the Constitution Amendment Bill in Parliament involving delimitation. While the floor leaders of the I.N.D.I.A. bloc parties will be present at the meeting, the non-I.N.D.I.A. bloc parties such as the DMK, the AAP and the BJD, among others, have also been invited for the discussions. 7. What is the government's argument for using the 2011 Census? Union Home Minister Amit Shah had argued in the Lok Sabha in April that a delimitation exercise undertaken after a fresh census will take time and delay an early implementation of the women's quota law. It will not be possible before the 2029 elections, given the extensive public consultations involved, he argued.

articles.title: Opposition parties slam Union govt's move to push delimitation Bill in Parliament
articles.summary: Opposition leaders across state and party lines have slammed the Union government’s move to convene a special sitting of Parliament on November 30 to push through the proposed delimitation Bill, warning that the exercise could undermine democratic representation and alter the country’s political balance. The move was defeated once before, in April 2026, when the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)-led government tabled the Constitution (131st amendment) Bill to expand the strength of the Lok Sabha from 543 to 850 members. This was during a special session convened while election campaigns were underway in several states. With the political atmosphere having changed since the election results were declared, the BJP hopes to get the required two-thirds majority of those present and voting. Even as opposition parties, including the Congress, remain steadfastly opposed to the proposed delimitation Bill, the stance taken by regional parties such as the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) and NCP will prove crucial to the BJP government. DMK awaits delimitation bill draft, wary of BJP’s assurances on 50% seat increase Responding to the development, Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD)’s Rajya Sabha MP Manoj Kumar Jha alleged that the proposed delimitation exercise raised concerns about politically motivated gerrymandering in the country. “The deeper concern is the possibility of politically motivated gerrymandering, carried out to suit the whims and electoral interests of Narendra Modi ji and Amit Shah ji, along the lines of what was witnessed in Assam. Such an exercise, if driven by partisan considerations rather than constitutional principles and democratic fairness, could seriously undermine representative democracy, federal balance and national unity. Aren’t you worried?” he wrote on X. Congress veteran P Chidambaram called the BJP government’s linking of women’s reservation in Parliament to the delimitation exercise as malicious and mischievous. “The Constitution (106th) Amendment Act inserted Article 334A which tied women's reservation to delimitation after the next Census … Congress and other Opposition parties opposed the insertion of Article 334A which, unnecessarily, created two hurdles: Census and Delimitation after the Census. But the BJP was adamant and insistent on Article 334A. Mischievously. Maliciously. The Bill was passed and became a law including Article 334A. All that the BJP has to do is propose to delete Article 334A. Once Article 334A is deleted, women's reservation can be implemented immediately,” his X post read. Trinamool Congress (TMC) MP Sagarika Ghosh questioned the Union government’s earnestness in implementing women’s reservation in Parliament, which is a legislation that has been tied to the delimitation exercise. “If Modi-(Amit Shah) were serious about representation of women, why has the law for women’s reservation — ALREADY UNANIMOUSLY PASSED in 2023—not been implemented? The Delimitation Bill is nothing but a SHAMELESS POWER GRAB wrapped in a sari. It not only reveals the (BJP India)’s contempt for democracy, but also the BJP’s hatred and contempt for women,” she alleged. Sagarika also raised questions about whether 20 TMC MPs who defected following the party’s defeat in the 2026 West Bengal Assembly elections would be allowed to vote on the Bill. “For 6 months (the Lok Sabha Speaker) has NOT RULED on the 20 TRAITOR TMC MPs against whom Disqualification Petitions are pending. Even Supreme Court directives have gone unheeded. Will these traitors now be allowed to vote on the Delimitation Bill in the Lok Sabha? Are their votes legal? How can they vote when they should have been disqualified by now?” she questioned. Referring to the defections by opposition party MPs, Congress leader Jairam Ramesh said the Modi government has pinned its hopes on a “super-tainted” majority. “...[A]fter 105 days of Operation Lotus, the Modi Govt announces a special session, hoping that it will get its super-tainted two-thirds majority to pass a Constitution amendment bill. Can there be a great insult to and assault on the Constitution? The fight is on,” he stated . Stating that the Congress will not let the delimitation law pass in Parliament, Congress leader KC Venugopal accused the Union government of attempting “Sansad chori”. He said , “They are Vote Chors . They are Seat Chors . There is no doubt that their Delimitation Bill will be nothing more than an exercise in Sansad Chori .” “‘Delimitation’ will prove to be the biggest mistake in the BJP’s politics,” said Akhilesh Yadav, leader of the Samajwadi Party (SP). His state of Uttar Pradesh, which is slated to go to polls in 2027, is expected to have the highest increase in Lok Sabha seats with the delimitation exercise. Shiv Sena (UBT) leader and MP Sanjay Raut called delimitation a conspiracy by the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). In an X post, he said , “Delimitation is a BJP conspiracy to strip the people of this country of their power. Anyone who supports it is betraying the people of this country. They will be known as the biggest traitors of the 21st century. Therefore, every patriotic, democratic party should reject delimitation in Parliament. History always remembers the names of traitors, explanations for betrayal fade into thin air.”
